message.content: Norman architecture is described as a unique Romanesque idiom characterized by rounded arches (particularly over windows and doorways), massive proportions, and the encastellation of regions with keeps in the north French style. It spread to England and Italy, immediately succeeding Anglo-Saxon architecture in England and preceding Early Gothic. In southern Italy, the Normans incorporated Islamic, Lombard, and Byzantine building techniques, initiating a distinctive Norman-Arab style within the Kingdom of Sicily.
